_doc: The vector stars drawn over a nebula sky, and how they streak (nebula-skies design 5). Each star is a direction at infinity; every frame it is drawn as a line from where it is on screen now back toward where it was tail_s ago, so a turning view smears the stars into short lines (FreeSpace's way: the star's last position kept, a line drawn to it, its length capped and its brightness dimmed as it grows). A star's class sets its brightness range (the sky file holds each star's own) and its head's size at rest; its colour is a tint. streak: tail_s the seconds of turning a tail shows, max_deg the longest tail (angle), min_px the least line drawn (a star at rest is a point), dim_per_deg the brightness lost per degree of tail (FreeSpace 2's 7,800 per unit) and dim_floor the least kept (FreeSpace 2 kept 75 of 255 over black space; 0.5 here so a streak still reads over a bright cloud), tail_fade the tail end's share of the head's opacity, alpha_min and whiten: a star is alpha-blended (FreeSpace's alpha-blended lines) toward its colour mixed whiten of the way to white, at an opacity of alpha_min + (1 - alpha_min) x its brightness, times the dim, cut_deg_s a turn faster than this is a camera cut (no tail that frame), faint_floor the faint hashed stars' brightness while the tail is at its cap (design 5.5: they fade during a fast turn). motes: patrol-mission 11.4's dust round the eye, drawn by the same streak rule from eye-space points, so moving forward fast shows. Colours sRGB 0-1.
